In addition to blog posts, 
I want a new content type 

one where we have books 
each book has a series of chapters like 1, 2, 3 etc 
each chapter has sub chapters
each subchapter has specific information 
and is followed by a series of multiple choice questions 
sometimes a question has a single correct answer 
sometimes a question has multiple correct answers
so far I believe all of this can be done without a backend 
use the browser's indexed db or something to keep track of progress 

but still we should write resilient code 
and not crash if the backend is unavailable
but if it is available we will do the same thing with 
analytics service to show readers on the page

as we do all of this 
please be mindful to use best engineering practices 
and solid principles 

Use your best judgment
If only a few files (under five or there about) need to change, give me the full path of the files that need to change and the FULL file 
if there are a lot of files that need to change

    do not include any file that has not changed

I’ve built the books feature with chapters, subchapters, quizzes and saved progress. It’s packaged as one archive of changed and new files only (71 files). I couldn’t compile or run the tests: this sandbox has no network route to the .NET SDK. Please run dotnet test before you merge, since warnings are treated as errors and a stray nullable warning would fail the build.

Delivery: from the repo root, run tar -xzf terlingua-books.tar.gz --strip-components=1. Nothing needs to be deleted.

Writing a book

Each book is a folder under content/books/: book.yml, then folders like 01-chapter/ containing chapter.yml and files like 01-subchapter.md.
The questions go in each subchapter’s front matter. Single- or multiple-answer is worked out from how many options are marked correct, or you can set type: multiple to show checkboxes even when only one answer is right.
Questions, options and explanations can use Markdown.
Bad content stops the build with a list of errors instead of shipping silently. That covers a question with no correct answer, unnumbered files, a missing chapter.yml, bad YAML and duplicate ids. The sample book blazor-basics shows the format.
Progress, without a backend

Progress is saved per book in IndexedDB. If IndexedDB is blocked or hangs, the app switches to in-memory storage for the session and tells the reader progress won’t be kept. Corrupt or old saved data is thrown away rather than crashing the page.
A section counts as complete when every question has been answered correctly, or when it’s opened if it has no questions.
The book page shows a progress bar, ✓/◐/○ status per section, “Continue reading” and a two-step reset. The reader page has the quiz, a “Try again” / “Show answer” flow, and previous/next links that cross chapter boundaries.
Analytics, when the backend is up

I reused the existing view-count endpoints with keys like book--{slug}, so the backend doesn’t need any changes.
A reader is counted once per book and once per section, using the saved progress to avoid counting repeat visits. Quiz answers are sent as interaction events.
If the backend is down, the reader counts just don’t appear.
Changes to existing code

Shared content component: the blog post’s content styling and syntax highlighting moved into a new RichContent component, so books and blog posts render the same way. BlogPost.razor and its CSS are smaller as a result.
Tests now use the real code: the integration test project now references the content processor directly instead of copying its logic. The existing blog tests still use their copies; I left them alone.
Front matter parsing: the closing --- now has to be at the start of a line, so a title like a---b no longer breaks parsing. This applies to blog posts too.
Smaller edits:
“Books” link in the nav menu and a card on the home page.
Explicit --books-dir in both workflows.
book-data/ added to .gitignore.
A README section on writing books.
New tests cover quiz grading, progress calculation, the storage fallback, loading book data, the quiz card UI and the build-time compiler.

Files are in /mnt/user-data/outputs:

terlingua-books.tar.gz
